findings.claim: In the touch layout, a scrub started from bottom-only while the player is paused immediately turns the chrome into the whole chrome, because the auto-hide effect re-runs on the `scrubbing` change and clears bottom-only whenever `paused` is true.
findings.impact: A viewer pauses, double-taps to skip (bottom-only), then drags the seek bar. The centre play button and the top-right buttons appear at the start of the drag instead of staying hidden until 2 s after the scrub ends. The spec's step 5 says a scrub started in bottom-only stays bottom-only. Nothing is lost: the chrome would have turned whole 2 s later anyway, because the player is paused.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/player/MediaControls/hooks/useMediaControlsState.ts:222-234: the effect `if (paused || holdVisible) setBottomOnly(false)` has deps `[paused, scrubbing, holdVisible, autoHideMs, revealNonce]`, so beginScrub (line 279-282, setScrubTime) re-runs it while paused and clears bottomOnly. The separate paused-transition effect at 238-242 already handles pause and resume, so the `paused` half of line 223 matters only when the effect re-runs for an unrelated dep. watchedBand.visibility.test.tsx 'a scrub started in bottom-only stays there...' uses only a playing stub (paused false), so this path is untested.
findings.repro: not_reproduced (read only). Steps: touchPage({ paused: true }); doubleTap(); expect chrome() 'bottom-only'; pointerDown on the Seek slider (touch). By reading, chrome() then returns 'whole'.

bucket_proposal.reason: I5 limits what takes touches while the chrome is in bottom-only and says the chrome is whole while paused after the window. It does not say a scrub keeps bottom-only, so no declared invariant is broken. The behaviour differs from Normal flow step 5.

findings.proposed_fix: Clear bottomOnly in that effect only for holdVisible, and leave pause and resume to the dedicated paused-transition effect. Add a paused variant of the scrub-in-bottom-only test.

specification_compliance: Fix commit f94a4efe moves `_attach_watched_ranges(db, viewer_id, response.shelves)` inside the `try` in `_shelves` (backend/app/routers/shelves.py:544). A failure of the watched_ranges query now goes through the existing `logger.exception("Shelves failed: ...")` handler and is re-raised as a 500. This matches the failure table ('as any other query failure in the handler') and resolves the logging gap raised in r1 (R2's side note and the unspecified_behavior item).
The fix changes no output: the attach call runs after the response is built on both branches, and its effect on successful requests is unchanged, so I9 (files, order, counts) is unaffected.

New test test_spec_core_141_a_failed_ranges_query_on_shelves_is_logged_like_any_shelves_failure (backend/tests/test_watched_ranges.py) drops played_segments and asserts a 500 and a 'Shelves failed' record. Mutation: moving the call back after the except would leave the 500 but drop the log record, so this test kills it.
r1's R1 (CardProgress.tsx not in the touch points) and R2's dispatch-refactor point are not addressed by this commit. Both were bucket B with no code defect.
potential_unspecified_behavior: The r1 item about `focus-within:opacity-100` being replaced with `has-[:focus-visible]:opacity-100` in TouchControlsPresenter.tsx:109 is unchanged by this commit. The code comment gives the reason: a tap leaves focus on the pressed button, which would otherwise hold the bar on screen.
regression_risks: Watch-history (drives.py:1793) still calls watched_ranges_by_file outside any try/log wrapper. That is consistent with the rest of that handler, which has no such wrapper, so a failure there is still only the framework's 500 log.

Inside the try, any exception from `_attach_watched_ranges` (including a serialization or attribute error) is now logged as 'Shelves failed' before re-raising. This is intended and does not change status codes.
test_coverage: The new caplog test covers the fix's only behavioural change, the log line on shelves. The pre-existing 500/no-write test covers the status.
watchedBand.visibility.test.tsx covers bottom-only scrubbing only while playing. The paused variant (R1) is untested.

The backend tests cover unkeyed by=watch shelves, shelves/query and watch-history. Keyed shelves (key=continue, key with page) through `_attach_watched_ranges` are not exercised by test_watched_ranges.py.
